# ARGUS 2027 build progress

The build session's log. Feature and gate status live in `docs/build/features.json`; read them with `python3 tools/build_ledger.py summary`. The live copies of both files are on the integration branch `platform/build-2027`; `main` keeps the starting copies until the build ends. How the session works is in `docs/build/SESSION.md`.

## Decisions made during the build

Choices the specs did not settle, with the reason. Newest first.

| Date | Feature | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | `argus_camera` has no flag: it is a new package whose node runs only when its own launch file is started. The 2026 grabbers and their launch files are not touched and nothing shipped starts the new node | A flag would have nothing to switch: with everything off the package is not running. Its `legacy_topics` parameter (default true) is what lets the 2026 detector run on it when someone does start it |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | Frames are read through OpenCV's capture (a GStreamer pipeline for CSI, V4L2 for USB), as the 2026 grabber does. A frame's capture time is the clock when it comes out of the driver, until FND-01 | It is what is on the Jetson image today and needs no new dependency. Reading the buffer's own timestamp needs the GStreamer bindings, which is FND-01's work in `capture_clock.py` |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | Calibration files: `imx519_4k` is the measured 2026 one; `imx519_720p60` is the 4K numbers divided by three, marked `measured: false` (the node warns); `ov9782_flow` has none and the node refuses it; the 12 MP spare is not listed | "K and D measured in that mode" needs the bench. The scaled 720p file is what 2026 flew, kept so the mode can run, and labelled so nobody mistakes it for a calibration. Nothing in the repo says which sensor the spare is |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | `config/robot.yaml` holds named airframes. `argus_2027` (not verified): camera 0.2667 m forward, 0.03 m right, 0.40 m below the flight controller, from `mission_logger`'s parameters; image top toward the nose, from the sequences' `camera_yaw_offset_deg: 0`; payload offset zero. `sim_iris_downcam` (verified against the sim model). Cameras are described as looking straight down with an image yaw only | The 2026 copies disagree: `mission_logger` has `mount_yaw: 180`, the sequences have 0, and only `mission_logger` has a lever arm. The centring that flew used 0. A person has to measure; a tilted mount would need a fuller rotation than this file has |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | `imx519_4k` and `ov9782_flow` are `in_process_only`: the node refuses to publish them. Topics are `/argus/camera/<camera>/image_raw` and `camera_info`, plus the 2026 names as aliases | Decision 5 of the brief: no 4K images over ROS topics, and the flow camera is read in-process |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | In the sim the node relays the bridged Gazebo camera (`ros_topic` mode) and was run beside the sim; the sim's missions still read the bridge directly | Routing the missions through the node means changing the bridge's topic names per sensor profile, which is SIM-05's camera-profile work. FND-01's sim test needs only the stamps, which the relay passes through |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-03 | The frame log core writes lossless PNG frames and an `index.jsonl`, can thin by time and stops at a size limit. When to log is left to LOC-11 | "The frame logger core lives here"; the policy has its own feature |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | The stale-data guard stays off in `delivery/time_base` after all (this replaces "PLT-06 adds it" below). The scenario is back in the nightly suite | With pose at 30 Hz the guard no longer trips on pose age, but flown with it on the delivery never got down: 17 trips on frame age, 250 to 282 ms against the 250 ms limit, each a hold of 1 to 5 s, and the recovery climbs used up. On a club laptop a frame is that old by the time the mission can use its detection. FND-01 and PLT-03 own the camera and detector timing; whichever brings it under the limit adds the flag. Without the guard the scenario now passes with margin (stamps within 5 ms at p95) |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | The stream keeper is switched by a launch argument, `stream_keeper:=false` by default, on `config/mavros/argus_mavros.launch.py`. The plugin allow-list and time sync have no switch of their own: using that launch file at all is the opt-in | A node that is not started cannot read a `features.` parameter. The 2026 start-up (`mavros_boot.sh`, MAVROS's `apm.launch`) is untouched and is what flies with everything off; PLT-07's bringup passes the argument from the profile |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | Rates held: `LOCAL_POSITION_NED` 30 Hz (pose), `ATTITUDE` 50 Hz, `RANGEFINDER` 20 Hz, `GPS_RAW_INT` 5 Hz, `BATTERY_STATUS` 2 Hz; and, beyond the spec's five, `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT` 20 Hz, `EXTENDED_SYS_STATE` 2 Hz and `SYS_STATUS` 2 Hz | The spec names quantities, not messages; "GPS 5 Hz" is read as the receiver's message. The other three are held at what the 2026 start-up gives them (`simple_takeoff_service`: all streams at 20 Hz, landed state at 2 Hz). The missions take their hold points from `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`, so holding it at 5 Hz would have made that fix up to 200 ms old where 2026 has 50 ms; the landed state would not come back after a reboot; and nothing else requests `SYS_STATUS` (the pre-arm bit) on a link of MAVROS's own (flight-guardian). ArduPilot's `RANGEFINDER` is what MAVROS's `rangefinder` plugin reads; `DISTANCE_SENSOR` joins if CEN-03 uses the `distance_sensor` plugin |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | The keeper requests every rate on connection, after a reboot (MAVROS reconnecting, or the flight controller's clock on `/mavros/timesync_status` going back by more than 1 s), and every 10 s regardless. It sends `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` through `/mavros/cmd/command`, one request at a time, gives an unanswered one up after 6 s, asks for nothing for 5 s after a failure, and then asks for the other messages before the failed one | The spec asks only for the reboot. The repeat is needed in every mission: `simple_takeoff_service` asks for all streams at 20 Hz when a mission starts, which replaces ours. It is also what restored the rates after a SITL reboot, where neither reboot signal shows (SITL takes its clock from Gazebo, and MAVROS did not report a disconnect). One at a time, because the first version sent all of them together every 5 s through MAVROS's `set_message_interval` service and the MAVROS log showed runs of 55 `set_message_interval service timeout` errors a second apart, through an RTL and landing: that service blocks the callback group that also serves `set_mode` for 1 s per call, and MAVROS's command plugin serves all commands, the gripper's included, in turn with a 5 s acknowledgement wait |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | On sim time MAVROS connects straight to SITL's second serial port (TCP 5762) instead of MAVProxy's UDP output. The default sim is unchanged | Through MAVProxy poses came at 4 Hz whatever was requested (MAVProxy's own stream requests replace ours every few seconds) and pose stamps were 10 to 13 ms from the sim clock at the median; direct, 30 Hz and 1 to 2 ms. It is also how the aircraft is wired. Cost: MAVROS does not reconnect a TCP link, so a SITL reboot in this mode ends the sim's MAVROS |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | The allow-list is the twelve plugins the repo uses today, checked both ways by a test. `param`, `waypoint` and `distance_sensor` are not loaded | "Only the plugins we use." Nothing reads flight-controller parameters or uploads missions through MAVROS yet (the GPS harness and the fence tools use pymavlink); PLT-13 and CEN-03 add their plugin when they use it. The ROS graph in a flight goes from 65 nodes to 23 |
| 2026-11-17 | PLT-06 | `sim/rate_check.py` passes a topic at 90% of its requested rate, treats the rangefinder as optional when silent, and runs beside every sim-time flight; a failed or missing rate check makes the run INVALID | ArduPilot rounds intervals to its loop rate, and the takeoff service's request leaves pose and attitude at 20 Hz for up to 10 s, until the keeper's next pass (a flight counted for under a minute could fail on attitude for that reason; the 160 s delivery has margin). A vehicle without a rangefinder sends none. Without a check in the flight nothing would notice pose falling back to 4 Hz |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | The time check compares pose stamps with Gazebo's own clock, read directly, not with `/clock` as a ROS subscriber receives it. `delivery/time_base` is out of the nightly suite until it passes reliably | `/clock` is that clock, one message in four; reading it in Python put 250 callbacks a second ahead of every pose. It did not change the result (23.0 ms before, 23.9 ms after), so the checker is not what holds the figure above 20 ms. A scenario that is INVALID two times in three would fail every nightly run |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | With the guard on, a target-recovery climb gives up (the mission fails) once the time base has been UNHEALTHY for `time_guard_hold_timeout_s` | With a dead pose stream the 2026 recovery waits for a climb it can never see finish, and the failure policy never fires (flight-guardian, round 2) |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | `/clock` is bridged by our own `sim/clock_bridge.py`, one message per 4 ms of sim time, not by `ros_gz_bridge` | `ros_gz_bridge` passes on all 1000 clock messages per sim second and cannot thin them. Every node on sim time handles each one, and MAVROS is about sixty nodes: measured, MAVROS took 280% of a core, each Python node 60%, and the flight ran at 0.55 of real time |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | The `delivery/time_base` scenario does not turn `time_health_guard` on; PLT-06 adds it. FND-03's sim proof is the time check; the guard is proven by unit tests through the real missions and executor | The first flight with the guard on held all the way (`pose is 145 ms old`): the sim delivers poses at 4 Hz in sim time, whatever `simple_takeoff_service` requests, against a 100 ms limit. PLT-06's stream keeper is what holds pose at 30 Hz |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | Sim time is opt-in: `SIM_TIME=1 sim/run_sim.sh` by hand, `sim_time: true` in a scenario (variant on only), `use_sim_time:=true` on a mission launch. The default sim and every flags-off flight stay on the wall clock | "All flags off flies exactly as `comp-2026`", and G0 and its re-checks measure the flags-off sim as it was. A later feature whose proof depends on timing sets `sim_time: true` in its scenario; the lead can make it the default once G0-W2 has passed with it |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | "Pose stamps agree with `/clock` within 20 ms" is judged on the 95th percentile of the absolute difference over the flight, with at least 100 poses; the maximum is reported, not judged. At least 100 stamps must also be synchronised flight-controller time (a whole number of milliseconds plus MAVROS's offset), so the check cannot pass on arrival-time stamps | One late message on a loaded laptop should not fail a ten-minute run. Arrival-time stamps agree with `/clock` whatever the link does, and MAVROS uses them until its filter has converged, so agreement alone would prove nothing |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | The sim's start script waits (up to 300 s) for MAVROS's time sync to be applied before READY when on sim time | MAVROS 2.16 applies its offset only after 500 samples, and on sim time its first windows are spoiled: SITL's clock starts equal to Gazebo's, the offset is near zero, and MAVROS's unsigned arithmetic turns a slightly negative offset into a huge one. It recovers by itself once SITL's clock has fallen a few ms behind (about two minutes); see `docs/results/2026-11-17-time-base.md` |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | `config/mavros/argus_mavros.yaml` holds only the `sys_time` block for now, and `config/mavros/argus_mavros.launch.py` loads it after MAVROS's own `apm_config.yaml`. `mavros_boot.sh` is untouched | FND-03 needs the file to prove its requirement in the sim before PLT-06 fills it. Note for PLT-06: MAVROS 2.16's `apm_config.yaml` already sets `timesync_rate: 10.0`; the 0 in the spec is the plugin's own default, used when no config sets it |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | The guard's "frame age" is the age of the newest `/drone_package_drop/target_detection` stamp. A new node flag on the detector, `features.stamp_from_image` (default false, declared in its five params files), makes that stamp the image's own instead of the detector's clock | The detection is the only per-frame message the executor receives. With the 2026 stamp the guard would only see a stopped camera or detector, never a late frame (flight-guardian blocker). In the sim the image stamp is Gazebo's render time; on the aircraft it is the grabber's publish time until FND-01 makes it the capture time, and FND-01 takes this flag over |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | Beyond the three limits in the spec, the guard also reads UNHEALTHY when a pose, a frame or the time-sync status has never arrived, when time sync has been silent for 2 s, for 1 s after an offset jump, when a stamp is ahead of the clock by more than its limit, and when no pose in the last 0.5 s carried synchronised flight-controller time. A mission's guard, once UNHEALTHY, stays so until the reports have been healthy for 1 s | Missing data must not read as healthy. Without time sync, and for the first minute after MAVROS starts or its filter resets, MAVROS stamps poses on arrival and the pose-age check sees nothing. Stamps made around a jump are still in use for a moment after it. The 1 s of hysteresis makes a flickering time base one long fault instead of a stall that never times out |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | With the guard on, the 2026 drop and delivery missions also stop their blind column descent while UNHEALTHY: they hold the column's point at the vehicle's own height (not the column's lower setpoint) and fail after `time_guard_hold_timeout_s` (new key, default 10 s) so the failure policy acts. A delivery already on the ground finishes its touchdown | "Hold, never descend" covers the one descent that does not use the target. Without a timeout a dead camera would leave the vehicle hovering until the battery failsafe |
| 2026-11-17 | FND-03 | On sim time a run is not held to the 0.8 real-time rule; it must pass its time check instead | SIM-07: the rule stands "until every node runs on sim time", and the time check shows each node did |
| 2026-11-15 | SETUP-1 | `argus_interfaces` has the four definitions exactly as the spec lists them, with no extra fields. Its `package.xml` copies the maintainer and the licence line of the other packages (the licence line still reads "TODO: License declaration", as theirs do) | Later features add fields and record it here. Who maintains the package and under what licence is the lead's to set for the whole repo; the session will not invent either |
| 2026-11-15 | SETUP-1 | `MarkerTrack.digit` is a plain `int8` with no default in the file, so a new message has digit 0, not −1: a publisher must set −1 itself when the digit is unknown | The spec gives the field as `int8 digit` (−1 when unknown), not as a field with a default; LOC-7, the first publisher, owns setting it |
| 2026-11-15 | FND-09 | The set-down release ceiling is 1.82 m, not 1.83: 6 ft is 1.8288 m, and a ceiling rounds down where the drop's floor (1.83) rounds up. Heights given to the module are above the ground under the vehicle, never altitude above home. A height request that is not a finite number raises instead of returning the floor | From the flight-guardian's review: a ceiling rounded up allows a release 1.2 mm over the rule; a home-relative altitude is wrong by the terrain difference; and returning the floor would turn a broken estimate into a commanded descent, where raising makes the mission fail and its failure policy act |
| 2026-11-15 | FND-09 | The load-time check tests a drop against the 1.83 m rule, not our own 2.0 m floor, and it models when the 2026 drop mission starts its drop (altitude minus tolerance): it does not see the ground height at the target or what the aircraft does during the hover. The check is a necessary condition, written so nobody reads a pass as proof of a legal drop |
